title.zh: 块、文件与对象存储：NAS 和 SAN 的分别
title.en: Block, file and object storage: how NAS and SAN differ

description.zh: 客户端向对面要的是块、文件里的字节还是整个对象，决定了谁管文件系统、能不能共享。
description.en: Whether a client asks for blocks, bytes of a file or whole objects decides who runs the file system and what can be shared.

zh: 块存储 文件存储 对象存储 区别
两台电脑能挂同一块 iSCSI 盘吗
en: block vs file vs object storage

title.zh: NAS 的文件协议：NFS、SMB 与小文件的往返
title.en: NAS file protocols: NFS, SMB and small-file round trips

description.zh: 每个文件都要和服务器问几次，往返时间乘上文件数，就是小文件拷得慢的原因。
description.en: Every file costs a few round trips to the server; round-trip time times the number of files is why small files copy slowly.

zh: 为什么从 NAS 拷小文件很慢
网络共享文件夹为什么慢
en: what protocol does a NAS use
why copying small files from a NAS is slow

title.zh: iSCSI：SCSI 命令走 TCP，写要等 R2T
title.en: iSCSI: SCSI commands over TCP, writes wait for R2T

description.zh: iSCSI 把 SCSI 命令装进 48 字节的包头，写入要等目标端的 R2T，往返越长等得越久。
description.en: iSCSI wraps SCSI commands in a 48-byte header; writes wait for the target's R2T, and longer round trips mean longer waits.

title.zh: 光纤通道的缓冲区信用与距离
title.en: Fibre Channel buffer-to-buffer credits and distance

description.zh: 光纤通道按对方空缓冲区的数目发帧，从不丢包；距离越长、速率越高，要的信用越多。
description.en: Fibre Channel sends only as many frames as the receiver has free buffers, so it never drops them; longer and faster links need more credits.

zh: 光纤通道为什么不丢包
光纤通道长距离要多少信用

title.zh: 网络存储的延迟账：介质、协议栈、光纤与交换机
title.en: The latency budget of network storage

description.zh: 盘快到几十微秒时，网络协议栈加的十几到二十几微秒就成了延迟的大头。
description.en: Once a drive answers in tens of microseconds, the network stack's added 5 to 20 microseconds becomes the largest part of the latency.

zh: NVMe over TCP 延迟多少
存储网络延迟由什么组成
en: how much latency does a network add to storage

title.zh: RDMA、RoCE v2 与无损以太网
title.en: RDMA, RoCE v2 and lossless Ethernet

description.zh: RDMA 绕开操作系统直接写对方内存，但常见网卡丢一个包就回退重发，所以要求以太网不丢包。
description.en: RDMA writes straight into the peer's memory without the OS, but common NICs go back N on a loss, so they want an Ethernet that does not drop.

zh: 为什么 RDMA 怕丢包

description.zh: NVMe-oF 把本机 NVMe 的命令和完成项原样装进胶囊，经 TCP、RDMA 或光纤通道送到对面的队列。
description.en: NVMe-oF carries local NVMe's commands and completions unchanged in capsules over TCP, RDMA or Fibre Channel to queues on the far side.

title.zh: 多路径的分流与切换：ALUA 与 ANA
title.en: Splitting and failing over across paths: ALUA and ANA

description.zh: 平时只走最优路，忙时分一部分给次优路；平时负载太高，最优路一断剩下的路就接不住。
description.en: Use the optimized path in normal times and spill to the other under load; run too hot and the remaining path cannot carry a failover.

title.zh: 三副本与纠删码：空间、持久性与修理代价
title.en: Replication vs erasure coding: space, durability and repair

description.zh: RS(10,4) 只多 40% 空间就能扛四块坏盘，代价是修一块要读十块。
description.en: RS(10,4) survives four failures for 40% extra space, at the cost of reading ten blocks to repair one.

title.zh: 看到网络存储时问的三件事
title.en: Three questions to ask about network storage

description.zh: 借给你的是什么、一次请求几个来回、断了一条路接不接得住。
description.en: What you are lent, how many round trips a request takes, and whether the remaining path can carry a failure.

zh: SAN 和 NAS 规格怎么看
en: how to read network storage specs
questions to ask about network storage

reason.zh: 第 2 章展开第 1 章表里文件级的那一行：要的是文件里的字节，所以每个文件都要和服务器问几次。
reason.en: Chapter 2 expands the file-level row of chapter 1's table: the client asks for bytes of a file, so every file costs a few questions to the server.

reason.zh: 第 3 章展开第 1 章表里块级的 iSCSI：要的是编了号的块，文件系统留在客户端。
reason.en: Chapter 3 expands the block-level iSCSI row of chapter 1's table: the client asks for numbered blocks and keeps the file system itself.

label.zh: 同一次读写，换一种胶囊
label.en: The same I/O in different capsules

reason.zh: 第 7 章把第 3 章 iSCSI 的写入路径和 NVMe/TCP、NVMe/RDMA 的消息逐条对比。
reason.en: Chapter 7 compares chapter 3's iSCSI write path message by message with NVMe/TCP and NVMe/RDMA.

reason.zh: 第 6 章的 RDMA 省掉的，正是第 5 章延迟账里 TCP 和 RDMA 往返之间相差的那十几微秒。
reason.en: What RDMA saves in chapter 6 is the gap of a dozen or so microseconds between the TCP and RDMA round trips in chapter 5's latency budget.

label.en: The transport sets the round trip

reason.zh: 第 7 章的三种传输，对应第 5 章延迟账里实测的不同网络往返时间。
reason.en: The three transports of chapter 7 correspond to the different measured fabric round trips in chapter 5's latency budget.

reason.zh: 光纤通道用信用让发送方不发多（第 4 章）；RoCE 要求以太网用 PFC 暂停帧做到同样的不丢包（第 6 章）。
reason.en: Fibre Channel keeps senders from overrunning the receiver with credits (chapter 4); RoCE asks Ethernet for the same losslessness with PFC pause frames (chapter 6).

reason.zh: 第 1 章的协议表沿用《硬盘里到底是什么》第 7 章的分层：命令说什么，由什么运输，跑在什么线上。
reason.en: Chapter 1's protocol table uses the layers of chapter 7 of “What a Drive Is Made Of”: what the commands say, what carries them, and which wire they run on.

label.zh: 同一个 CDB 装进 iSCSI

reason.zh: 第 3 章不再重拼 CDB：《服务器硬盘为什么用 SAS》第 2 章已经把它装进 iSCSI 的 48 字节包头。
reason.en: Chapter 3 does not rebuild the CDB: chapter 2 of “Why Server Drives Use SAS” already places it in iSCSI's 48-byte header.

reason.zh: 第 8 章借用《服务器硬盘为什么用 SAS》第 4 章双路径的可用度，再看两条不一样好的路怎么分流量。
reason.en: Chapter 8 takes the two-path availability of chapter 4 of “Why Server Drives Use SAS” and asks how to split traffic between two unequal paths.

reason.zh: 第 5 章是《NVMe 为什么这么快》第 1 章的延迟拆解换到网线上：介质时间不变，多出来一段网络。
reason.en: Chapter 5 is chapter 1 of “Why NVMe Is So Fast” moved onto the network: the media time is the same, with a network leg added.

label.en: Stretching the queues across the network

reason.zh: NVMe-oF 把《NVMe 为什么这么快》第 4 章的提交队列和完成队列拉到对面，命令和完成项装进胶囊。
reason.en: NVMe-oF stretches the submission and completion queues of chapter 4 of “Why NVMe Is So Fast” across the network, with commands and completions carried in capsules.

reason.zh: 第 2 章小文件慢的原因是每个文件要等几次往返；往返时间由什么组成见《网络流》。
reason.en: Chapter 2's small files are slow because each waits for several round trips; what a round trip is made of is in “Network Flow”.

label.zh: 副本：存几份与怎样一致
label.en: Replicas: how many and how consistent

reason.zh: 第 9 章只算存几份、能丢几块；副本之间怎样保持一致是《分布式系统》讲的问题。
reason.en: Chapter 9 counts copies and how many may be lost; how the copies stay consistent is the question of “Distributed Systems”.
